ownedTypes.why: an import statement is read through the name-resolution layer (what a name means) or edited by the import tier; every other consumer asks TypeNameBinding / ImportBindings / TypeRefIndex instead of decoding the statement again

the compiler's facts are produced by TypedFactsProbe for the run host and read through two doors: FactsView (the facts against the project, the reach analyses) and FactsTypeOracle (the facts placed in a file's text now, the TypeOracle a structural rule asks); the other owners are parts of the facts layer a door builds or reads through, answering from the facts alone. A rule or an analysis naming CompilerFacts grows another facts reader
the call graph's own type and import resolution; outside the graph, members resolve through MemberLookup / SubtypeGraph and names through TypeNameBinding

the index host (CachingGrammarPlugin as SymbolIndexHost) builds and memoises every index once per run, and IndexScope is the one door onto it: a rule names the scope its question needs (report / resolution / widest / over an explicit file set) and asks there; a consumer building its own picks its own scope and pays a rebuild

grants: Renderer <= 70 members / 4100 lines: the Doc layout engine is ONE algorithm — 47 of its 48 non-hub members land in a single `hxq clusters` component (98%), because every fit probe, push and flush reads the same render state. S11 measured the only real seam, a 22-member width layer, and cutting it leaves 2383 lines behind.

WrapList <= 114 members / 4660 lines: one wrapping decision table, 80 of 94 non-hub members in one component (85%). The members are arms of a single policy keyed by construct, not collaborating objects; splitting them by call edges would move the arms and leave the dispatch.

NullFlow <= 100 members: one MaybeNull lattice plus its transfer functions — 50 of 52 non-hub members in one component (96%). A flow-sensitive dataflow analysis has no seam that is not the lattice itself.

FactsView <= 152 members: the owned-types door to the compiler facts: 75 public questions, so no split reaches the member threshold without forwarders, and every member reads the same `_table` / `_scope` / `truth` (C2, re-measured).

MemberReach <= 152 members / 3130 lines: one member-reach analysis: `hxq clusters` puts 105 of its 119 non-hub members in one component (88%), and that component holds every mutable field, at every hub count tried (C2).
TypedFactsWalk <= 103 members: one typed-facts traversal: 56 of 66 non-hub members in one component (85%), the one holding every mutable field, at every hub count tried (C2).
FunctionValueTypes <= 86 members: one function-value inference: 44 of 59 non-hub members in one component, the one holding every mutable field, and no hub count tried separates it (C2).
NullGuardedCode <= 63 members: one null-guard analysis: 35 of 43 non-hub members in one component (81%), the one holding every mutable field, at every hub count tried (C2).

CompilerFacts <= 78 members: C2 moved its node-record decoding out (`FactNodeRecords`) and its node-site queries (`FactSites`); every member left serves the one fact table and its caches and reads the same fields.
ReachGraph <= 98 members: C2 moved its library-call predicates out (`LibraryCalls`, `ReachProject.declarationOf`); every member left reads the graph growth state.
TypedFactsMacro <= 57 members: C2 moved its type-string printer out (`TypedFactsTypeStrings`); what is left is the fact-record writer, every member of it reading the same fields.

CallGraph <= 67 members: its members are the public question surface 86 files read (C2 and B9 measured it); N13 moved `collectEdges` out (`CallGraphEdges.collect`) and kept that surface unchanged on purpose.

RefShape <= 320 members / 3600 lines: the grammar vocabulary a plugin hands every check, one slot per seam a check reads, so it grows a slot at a time. A class only because, as a structure typedef (which this rule does not size), it outgrew the JVM constructor-argument limit (J0, docs/testing.md); nesting its slots in groups is the decomposition, and it moves the read of every consumer.
